..
Issued at 300 AM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

Currently-Today... KMLB radar imagery shows dry weather across 
east central Florida. GOES-19 satellite imagery and local 
observations indicate partly to mostly cloudy skies over east 
central Florida. Temperatures are currently in the mid 70s to low 
80s with dew points in the low to upper 70s. Analysis charts show 
the western fringe of the Bermuda high to the east of the local 
Atlantic waters, in addition to, a cold front over the western 
Atlantic and Deep South which extends from weak low pressure near
the northeastern US coast. 

Scattered to numerous generally slow east-southeast moving showers 
(~30-80% chance) and lightning storms are forecast to develop along 
and ahead a cold front across east central Florida into the 
afternoon and evening hours. The greatest chance for rain showers
and lightning storms is between 2PM-12AM with the highest chances
across areas from Melbourne to Lake Kissimmee northwards. 
Guidance shows MLCAPE up to 500-2,600J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 
10-30kts, PWATs up to 2.0"-2.5" (above the maximum percentile for 
the date at 2.39"), and 500mb temperatures at -5C to -4C this
afternoon. Like the past several days, the stronger storm 
potential is likely to be somewhat limited due to relatively warm 
temperatures aloft and cloud cover. However, the potential exists 
for a strong storm or two capable of occasional to frequent 
lightning, wind gusts up to 35-45mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 1-
3"+ in 60 minutes). Areas that observe heavy rainfall and 
repeated rounds of showers/lightning storms will have the 
potential to result in minor flooding of roadways and low-lying 
areas. Afternoon highs in the mid 80s to around 90s with heat 
index values in the mid 90s to 103F degrees are forecast. There is
a Moderate HeatRisk today which can affect those sensitive to 
heat without adequate cooling and hydration. 

Tuesday-Wednesday... A wet week is expected as a blocking pattern 
develops with high pressure (~1024mb over the Ohio 
Valley/northeastern US) upstream of broad low pressure that is 
expected to develop over the southwest Atlantic near the Volusia/ 
Brevard county coasts, as well as high pressure over the western 
Atlantic. The aforementioned cold front is expected to extend 
from the low and stall/meander between northern Florida, as well 
as the middle half of east central Florida through midweek. 
Numerous to widespread showers (60-90% chance) and lightning 
storms are forecast to develop each day with the highest chances 
generally during the afternoon and evening hours (12PM-2AM). 
Guidance shows moderate instability/CAPE values, moderate to high 
bulk shear, plenty of moisture (PWAT values towards the maximum 
percentile), and relatively warm temperatures aloft coupled with 
500mb PVA pivoting across east central Florida during the forecast
period. The aforementioned weather parameters are supportive of 
isolated to scattered strong storms capable of frequent lightning,
wind gusts up to 40-50mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 1-3"+ in 60 
minutes). Thus, the WPC has outlooked east central Florida in a 
Marginal Risk (level 1 out of 5) for excessive rainfall both days 
with the potential for slow moving showers/storms rainfall to result
in flooding of roadways, as well as low lying areas, especially 
in areas that observe repeated rounds. Additionally, north- 
northwest winds are forecast to increase on the backside of low 
pressure near the Volusia/Brevard county coasts by Wednesday 
afternoon at 15-20mph with gusts to 30-35mph over Volusia, 
northern Brevard, Seminole, and eastern Lake counties. Afternoon 
highs in the low to upper 80s with lows in the upper 60s to mid 
70s are forecast.

Thursday-Sunday... Deterministic models and LREF-clusters continue
to be in good agreement that the longwave trough over the Deep 
South will begin to fill on Thursday before the Atlantic ridge 
builds back over the state of Florida into Friday. The stationary 
boundary is forecast to meander over east central Florida and 
gradually lift north to northern Florida through the weekend. 
Therefore, rain chances remain above normal through the forecast 
period. Scattered to widespread showers (~50-90% chance) and 
lightning storms are forecast each day (slightly lower 
shower/storm chances on Sunday) with the greatest chances in the 
afternoon/evenings. Generally, seasonable to below normal high 
temperatures are forecast (warmest south of the front across 
southern east central Florida). Above normal low temperatures are 
forecast.
